a.caveats: 1) Single-minibatch losses (confirmed from game/imitate.py train_rows, lines 204-228): train_rows returns the list of per-minibatch losses (one float per optimiser step, MINIBATCH=256, EPOCHS=3, so ~99-123 values per round), and iteration_stats records loss_first=losses[0] (the first minibatch of epoch 1, computed BEFORE the first optimiser step on that batch, i.e. essentially the pre-update loss on one random 256-row batch) and loss_last=losses[-1] (the last minibatch of epoch 3, a PARTIAL batch of train_rows mod 256 rows, e.g. 96 rows when train_rows=9056, so even noisier). Each is one weighted cross-entropy on one random minibatch using normalised weights, not an epoch mean and not a held-out loss; the weights are normalised over the whole training set, so batch losses are heavy-tailed (a few high-weight rare-type rows swing a batch). The first/last differences (e.g. s200 r21 1.47 -> 0.34, s201 r23 1.31 -> 1.57) therefore cannot be read as fit or non-fit; they are noise-dominated. 2) Z5 uses new rows only; the actual training set is new rows plus an equal-size uniform sample from a 20,000-row buffer whose per-type composition (and per-row weight, stored from earlier rounds' weights) is not in the JSONs, so true training-weight shares differ from these. Buffer rows carry weights from the round they were created, and prune_buffer drops rows of types whose longest kept length shrank. 3) 'one-move types' = types whose longest_kept==1 in that round (all kept rows of that type are single-move segments); the set of such types changes per round (drink, plant, table always; stone/place_stone occasionally). 4) A27 loop uses rare_below>0 (types with fewer than rare_below segments keep all segments <=12 moves; I did not need the value for weights since weights depend on 'segments' counts only; I did not check the exact rare_below used by the A27 run). Weights use 'segments' (pre-keep) counts per imitate.py line 317 as the committed rule; floor = max weight/20 binds for most large types (sapling, plant, drink, wood). 5) Z4: played agreement counts views whose oracle label type is nav/act, computed on a sample of all played views (rows_all_sample), views 6.0-7.3k per round; sample sizes imply binomial SE of about 0.3 percentage points per round, so within-seed round-to-round differences of a few tenths of a point are mostly noise. Spearman p-values are two-sided permutation p's, n=8 and n=16, no multiplicity correction; rounds are sequentially dependent (one training chain per seed), so effective n is smaller than nominal and p-values are optimistic. Pooled correlation is confounded by the between-seed offset (seed 201 is higher on all three variables); the within-seed correlations are the cleaner read and are weak/inconsistent in sign. 6) A26 round 1/8/16 agreement values are only available as the single transcribed sentence above (round 1 kept 10%, round 8 kept 21-22%, played 6-9% for rounds 1-8 combined); no per-seed values and no round-16 value are stated anywhere I could find (grep of game/*.md), and the A26 per-round JSONs are not in game/results (only A27, A28-census, gwb, gwp8). 7) Nothing in the repo was modified; no game was played; no sealed world touched.
